subject: Order Form indemnity: routing, notice timing, and evidence requirements
messages:
From: Joe Brown <joe.brown@acme-corp.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.com
Cc: marta.ruiz@acme-corp.com, legal@acme-corp.com
Date: 2025-11-10 09:12 -0800
Subject: Order Form indemnity — proposed language and flow questions

Rachel —

Thanks for the demo last week. Attached is the redlined order form our procurement team circulated this morning. Two quick questions we want to clarify before routing to procurement:

1) Who owns defense/control for third-party IP claims that relate to outputs generated by the model (customer claim vs third-party patent)? Your order form references MSA §7 for indemnity but the redline appears to shift defense to the customer in some scenarios.

2) Evidence and notice timing: procurement wants a concrete SLA for notice plus a short list of the evidence you will require to validate a claim (so we can route requests internally).

We'd like to avoid a long back-and-forth — can you confirm Redwood’s proposed flow (defend-and-control vs reimburse) and what you need from Acme if a claim arises?

Attached: Acme_OrderForm_Proposed_Redlines.pdf

Joe
VP Product, Acme Corp
joe.brown@acme-corp.com
+1 415 555 0102

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: joe.brown@acme-corp.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2025-11-10 10:03 -0800
Subject: Re: Order Form indemnity — proposed language and flow questions

Hi Joe —

Thanks — I reviewed your PDF and looped in Kimberly (legal) and Karthik (VP Legal) to confirm. High-level responses below and a suggested next step to keep procurement moving:

- Defense/control: Our standard position is defend-and-control for third-party IP infringement claims that accuse Redwood’s model outputs as infringing. We accept customer cooperation obligations (reasonable assistance, prompt notice, and not settling without consent). However, we can be flexible on limited scenarios where the alleged infringement is clearly caused by customer-supplied content or instructions — those would be customer-defense scenarios.

- Evidence & notice: We propose 30 calendar days' notice from the date the customer receives the written claim, and a short evidence list: (1) the third-party complaint or takedown notice, (2) exact content/outputs at issue (URLs or transcript), (3) reproducible prompts and timestamps if available, and (4) contact info for the claimant. We’ll accept secure links to artifacts in lieu of attachments.

- Cap and insurance: Typically indemnity for IP is uncapped for defense, but we understand procurement needs predictability. Kimberly — are we prepared to propose a rebuttable cap tied to the order form value for Acme, or do we want a carveout for core IP claims?

Next step: I’m attaching our MSA redline excerpt (Redlines_MSA_v3.docx) with inline comments showing defend/control language and a short evidence checklist. If Acme accepts these bullets we can prepare a one-page mutual action plan and a 30-min call with procurement to close.

Thanks —
Rachel Kim
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com
+1 650 555 0199

Attachment: Redlines_MSA_v3.docx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2025-11-11 09:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order Form indemnity — proposed language and flow questions

Rachel / Karthik —

Quick legal read and suggested compromises we can offer to procurement:

1) Defense/Control: Keep defend-and-control language in MSA §7 with customer cooperation covenant. Add a narrowly drafted exception where the claim relates solely to customer-supplied training data or content (we can require customer to defend in that case).

2) Notice & evidence: 30 days' notice is reasonable; include an illustrative evidence list identical to what Rachel proposed. Add a provision that we may request additional technical artifacts (logs/KV cache excerpts) under an agreed discovery process — subject to confidentiality.

3) Cap: Propose a multi-tiered cap in the order form: (a) for IP claims caused by Redwood core model outputs, cap at 2x the annual order value up to $1M; (b) for claims arising from customer content, customer retains liability. This gives procurement predictability while preserving meaningful exposure for Redwood.

4) Insurance & Escalation: Require Acme to maintain commercial general liability and cyber insurance with Redwood named as additional insured for third-party IP claims, and provide certificate within 10 business days of signing. For any claim > $250k we want automatic escalation to VP Legal (karthik) for settlement authority.

I attached a markup (Redlines_MSA_v3.docx) with inline suggestions and a short playbook for evidence routing. Happy to convert the cap proposal into explicit order-form text if you want me to draft it.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Attachment: Redlines_MSA_v3.docx

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: joe.brown@acme-corp.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2025-11-12 11:20 -0800
Subject: Re: Order Form indemnity — proposed language and flow questions

Joe / Marta —

Appended below is a consolidated proposal from our side to replace the ambiguous paragraphs in your PDF. If these bullets are acceptable we’ll insert precise order-form language and route to procurement:

- Defense: Redwood will defend and control the defense of third-party claims alleging IP infringement by model outputs, subject to Customer’s reasonable cooperation. Redwood will not settle on Customer’s behalf without consent if settlement imposes obligations on Customer.

- Customer-caused claims: If the claim arises solely from Customer-fed data or instructions (including training assets or content uploaded by Customer), Customer shall defend and indemnify Redwood.

- Notice & Evidence: Customer must provide notice within 30 calendar days of receiving the claim and deliver the following evidence: (i) the complaint/takedown notice; (ii) representative outputs allegedly infringing (URLs or transcript); (iii) reproducible prompt text and timestamps where available; (iv) claimant contact details. Redwood may request limited technical artifacts under confidentiality (e.g., logs) to validate the claim.

- Cap & Insurance: For Acme we propose an order-form cap equal to 2x the annual committed spend for IP defense exposure, up to a $1,000,000 maximum. Acme will provide certificate of insurance listing Redwood as additional insured within 10 business days of execution.

- Escalation: Any claim likely to exceed $250,000 will be escalated to Redwood VP Legal (karthik.iyer@redwood.com) for settlement authority.

If Acme agrees to the principles above, Kimberly will draft exact order-form text and I’ll circulate a mutual action plan with a DocuSign link. If you prefer a short call, I can schedule 30 minutes tomorrow.

Best,
Rachel
